questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a great university in an english speaking country. I have always dreamed of going to Australia so this was the perfect oppertunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I was a bit confused with the emails, receiving information from University of Melbourne sometimes through my KU mail and sometimes through my Melb mail. However, UniMelb is really good at providing all information and the student councelling (stop 1) was absolutely phenomenal.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received help with student card, subjects, and time schedule.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit hectic finding accommodation but all right (not like Copenhagen) because Melbourne has so many exchange students and backpackers coming and going. I moved into a hostel to begin with and literally everyone there was in the same situation as me, exchange students looking for a place to stay. Most people (including me) found accommodation through the facebook group "Fairy Floss" - thats the way to go!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
DONT LIVE ON CAMPUS - it is extremely overpriced (like up to 10.000 kr. pr month for a dorm room with shared kitchen and bathroom) and mainly undergrats from Asia living there. The university makes it sound like it is the only possibility but that is just to make money. It is so much nicer to live in a real Melbourne shared house with other students. That is a great way to meet some Aussies as well and it is significantly cheaper.

I recommend the lower part of Brunswick (I lived there, good vibes and pretty grungy with plenty of bars, venues and restaurant), Fitzroy (just super cool and so much to do. The beer gardens and rooftop bars are so cozy), Carlton (right in the middle of where u will go out and close to campus), and Collingwood (so much life, very queer)

Prahran and South Yarra are probably my favorite neighborhoods but they are a bit further away from campus and public transport is not exaclty amazing if you are used to Copenhagen standards.

I paid 1050 $AUD (around 5000 kr./md) for a furnished room. That was all right but you might find something slightly cheaper depending on the location.

The CBD (where all the sky scrapers are) is located very central, however it is not a super nice area to stay and suffocatingly busy)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Public transport is bad (there are trams and busses but everything goes so slow). I bought a bike on the webpage Gumtree (an Aussie version of DBA) for around 100 $AUD. There are bike lanes on most streets, however the cars are not that used to bikes so you have to be very careful since they are not as good at looking out for bikes as they are in Copenhagen. AND is it mandatory to wear a helmet, otherwise you will get fined.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are so many things you need to be on top of, and the whole process was just super tiring and stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The study abroad student service. They were pretty helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got basically what I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to get things done as early as possible - because there is a lot of stuff going back and forth and every time you need a confirmation/answer/document/enrollment/etc. from either KU or the university abroad it takes time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was extremely good - but also surprisingly challenging. I learned more than I have done in any past semester. The workload is intense.

Comparing myself to the other exchange students on BA level, it seems like there is a huge gap in the academic level and work load from BA to MA. They did not have to study nearly as hard as me (just keep that in mind). I actually ended up dropping one subject in order to have time for all the fun stuff. After all, thats why you go abroad as well right!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one subject that was fairly easy and two really difficult ones. The workload is huge - so although the things might be easy you just have to do a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Your final grade is the result of your academic performance throughout the whole semester (all assignments and sometimes weekly multiple choice tests). Thus, the final exam might only count 50% of your grade while your work throughout the semester counts for the other 50%. Apart from that it is similar with a couple of lectures and classes every week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Machine learning applications for health, computer vision, and algorithms for bioinformatics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Computer vision! Really challenging but so much fun. I learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: VISA is about 3.200 kr., and you need and overseas student health cover which is around 1400 kr. (depending on the insurance company)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol is pretty expensive apart from wine (which you can get very very cheap), cigarettes are extremely expensive (50$AUD for a pack), fruits and vegetables depends on the season but in general the super markets are like Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a gym on campus I used. Fairly cheap and really good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think basically anything you can imagine. However, I did not engage in too much of the uni activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I just used to gym but if you like that, its pretty good :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Close to Melbourne: Phillip island, great ocean road, Mornington peninsula, the beach.
In Melbourne: 
Night life areas; Chapel st (Prahran), Brunswick st and Smith St (Fitzroy).
Check out: Naked for Satan, Revolver, Circuit, Sunday day drag show at the Osborne, Watch a footy match (a weird aussie kind of football game)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are more open and easy to become friends with

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their attitude towards strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Explore the city, go travel and dont care too much about spending money. It will be expensive anyway and its worth it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont know

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made for sure!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my partner

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
